mutations.because: Drop the refusal of a tombstone at or above `nextIndex`. That slot was never allocated, and with the tombstone encoding it is this schema's form of the "cursor sits below a live slot" fault (a live-index list would spell it `nextIndex` below the highest live index). Accepting it lets a document claim a delete of a creative the run never made, so occupancy and the cursor disagree about how many slots the campaign ever had.
command: refuses a tombstone above the cursor, naming the field

mutations.because: Drop the duplicate-tombstone refusal. A slot listed twice is a document that cannot be reasoned about by counting — |live| is no longer nextIndex - |tombstoned| — so any consumer that sizes the set from the two numbers is silently off by the number of repeats.
command: refuses a duplicate tombstone, naming the field

mutations.because: Make the loader materialise the derived default onto the record, the way SL-D6's `minDistance` clamp deliberately does a few lines above. It is the inverse of what occupancy needs: `parseBrief` returns this same record as the brief, so the editor would hold a block the file never had and the next Save would patch `occupancy` into the YAML — every existing campaign's document churning on first write, and a pre-SL1 brief no longer round-tripping unchanged.
command: a brief with no occupancy does not acquire one

mutations.because: Stop writing occupancy back out of the editor. `toBrief` rebuilds `variation` key by key and `patchBriefYaml`'s `patchNode` then deletes every key the rebuilt object no longer names, so the operator's first Save of a campaign with occupancy would strip the block from their YAML — and with it every tombstone, resurrecting each deleted creative on the next run.
command: an edit to another field keeps occupancy byte-for-byte through save

mutations.because: Let a tombstoned index back into the live set. This is the recreate-on-delete bug restated at the schema level: the document still records the delete, but the resolved occupancy hands every caller the deleted slot as live, so SL2 would plan it and overwrite the tombstoned asset path.
command: a tombstoned index is never in the live set, for every tombstone shape

mutations.because: Fold occupancy into `policyHash` by the same conditional spread the anchor and headline axes use. The hash pins the draw POLICY so a selective re-roll is refused when the recipe moved underneath it; occupancy is the drawn set's state. Folded in, every delete moves the hash and refuses a re-roll of each SURVIVING creative — the exact property this plan exists to deliver. No golden can see this (none carries occupancy), and the whole policy-hash-stability suite stays green under it, so it needs its own claim.
